explanation: In C++, container iterator categories classify iterators based on the operations they support, which in turn determines how algorithms can interact with different container types. Understanding iterator categories (input, output, forward, bidirectional, random access) is essential for writing generic, efficient code that works seamlessly across various container types. These categories enable the use of appropriate algorithms and optimize performance by leveraging specific iterator capabilities.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how different container types (vector and list) have iterators categorized as random access and bidirectional, respectively. The function 'check_iterator_category' uses 'iterator_traits' to determine the iterator category at compile time and outputs the category name. This showcases how iterator categories classify container iterators, enabling generic programming and optimized algorithm selection based on iterator capabilities in modern C++.
